sentences.text: For the Appellant : Mr. K.P.Deo  For the State : A.P.P 05/ 27.01.15 . I.A.No.460 of 2015 Heard learned counsel appearing for the appellant and learned counsel appearing for the state.

Learned counsel appearing for the appellant submits that the appellant has preferred this appeal under Section 76 of the Food Safety and standard Act, 2006 against the order dated 2.9.2014 passed in F.S.S. case No.27 of 2013-14 whereby the appellant has been sentenced to pay fine of Rs.3,00,000/-.

While preferring the appeal, it was not known to the appellant about the court fee payable and therefore, submission was made to ask the counsel appearing for the State to get hold of a notification so that it could be known about the amount which is payable.
Meanwhile, a sum of Rs.25,000/- was ordered to be paid as court fee which has been paid by way of demand draft in the name of the Registrar General of this Court.

Subsequent to that, the appellant came to know that under Rule 11 of the Food Safety and Standard Rules, 2011 which does prescribe about the court fee payable over the amount of penalty, only a sum of Rs.2500/- is payable towards the amount of penalty of Rs.3,00,000/- and therefore, after deducting a sum of Rs.2500/-, rest of the amount be Laxman Mandal vs The State Of Jharkhand And Anr on 27 January, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/10232822/
1 ordered to be refunded to the appellant.
In view of the facts and circumstances as well as submission advanced on behalf of the appellant, let a sum of Rs.22,500/-be refunded to the appellant by way of demand draft and rest of the amount, i.e Rs.2500/- be kept as court fee payable towards penalty imposed, though payable to the Registrar,
Food and Safety Appellate Tribunal but since the Appellate Tribunal has not been functioning, the said amount be kept with this Court and be charged as court fee.
